objects.summary: Owner creates Codex re-entry checkpoint: post-cutoff context is stale until chronological remote replay; GitHub is brain, worker chats disposable CPU; no substantive action before compact REACQUISITION_ACK. F1 Stage A remains unobserved/unexecuted and acquisition lives in Claude-private scratchpad.
Owner re-entry pointer narrows Codex role to Research Lead/Convergence, delta-only remote reacquisition and one highest-VOI action; no new scout/implementation before ACK.
Owner explicitly wakes Codex and directs it to read the re-entry pointer.

Codex acknowledges rules and performs no mutation, but cannot verify remote GitHub because local gh is unauthenticated. Required remote reconstruction/ACK is therefore not complete; this is BLOCKED_REENTRY, not a successful reacquisition.
Owner says Claude is out of tokens and asks Codex to take over alone, with minimal acknowledgement to save tokens. Tool-availability continuity handoff, no new scientific/economic authority.
Owner tells Codex to continue and report eventually; this is wake/continuation instruction, not evidence of execution.

Codex resumes corrected F1 and tries Stage-A acquisition, but runtime network tunnel returns HTTP 403 before any download/outcome parse. Stage-A look remains intact; precise resume path is private acquisition or runtime with Binance Vision access, then one run.
Owner challenges Codex's ability to continue alone after another stop; evidence of perceived continuity failure, not a project result.

Codex takes solo decision-changing F1 action: forced exits now recalculate liquidity/cost at exit date; Stage B requires published Stage-A result SHA, harness identity and authenticated selected_theta. 24 tests pass; no outcome acquired/read and Stage-A look remains unconsumed.

cross_object_findings.finding: The historical re-entry protocol correctly requires remote reconstruction before action, but Codex could not satisfy it in its unauthenticated runtime. Acknowledging the rule is not the same as reacquiring remote state.
F1 acquisition existed in Claude-private scratchpad while Codex could not access Binance Vision; durable code/checkpoints were insufficient to transfer the actual acquired data state across runtimes.
Codex's HTTP 403 occurred before any outcome download/parsing; Stage-A economic look remained intact and should not be mislabeled failed/invalid experiment.

After Owner solo handoff, Codex identified and fixed two verdict-relevant F1 integrity/cost defects without consuming outcome data, showing useful solo progress is possible when the task is bounded and code-local.

GitHub state can preserve decisions/code, but scientific continuity also requires transferable acquisition/data artifacts or a reproducible accessible source; otherwise a fresh worker can know what to do yet still cannot execute it.
